description:
## Background

React Doctor reports two security warnings because `pnpm-workspace.yaml` does not delay newly published packages and does not prevent trust-signal downgrades between package versions. These controls reduce exposure to short-lived malicious releases and provenance weakening without changing application runtime behavior.

## What to build

Harden every repository install by configuring pnpm's release-age and trust-downgrade policies while preserving the existing native-build allowlist and `@wdio/native-utils` compatibility override.

## Technical Approach

- Add `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, representing seven days in minutes.
- Add `trustPolicy: no-downgrade`.
- Keep the existing `allowBuilds` and `overrides` semantics intact.
- Validate the settings with the repository-pinned pnpm version rather than weakening them when an existing lockfile entry lacks newly published metadata.

## Considerations

- A release-age policy can make an emergency dependency release temporarily unavailable; document any future exception narrowly rather than reducing the repository-wide delay.
- The existing lockfile should remain stable unless pnpm requires a metadata update. Do not perform unrelated dependency upgrades.
- This issue covers install-time supply-chain behavior only; it must not change application code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm-workspace.yaml` sets `minimumReleaseAge` to seven days.
- [ ] `pnpm-workspace.yaml` sets `trustPolicy` to `no-downgrade`.
- [ ] Existing build allowlists and dependency overrides remain effective.
- [ ] React Doctor no longer reports either `require-pnpm-hardening` warning.
- [ ] The canonical repository verification remains green.

## Test Plan

- Run `mise run doctor:react` and confirm both pnpm-hardening diagnostics are gone.
- Exercise a frozen install with the repository-pinned toolchain if lockfile validation is needed.
- Run `mise run verify`.
- No desktop E2E scenario is required because runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Triage
